decisions.reason: As a flagship product line very close to the core practice software, it likely meets strategic aspiration levels and the firm has reason to give it continued support despite some uncertainty.
The education institute builds on existing training and customer relationships, so even if direct returns are modest it likely remains acceptable within the firm's slack and complementary strategy.
A remote support tool fits tightly with the firm's service model and installed base, making it a low-risk complement that management would likely retain.
The analytics dashboard is newer and may still be below settled aspirations, but it is close enough to the core offer that management would likely continue it while learning and refining it.
A complete practice bundle is closely aligned with the firm's established business and likely supports cross-selling and customer lock-in, so dropping it would be unlikely.

Because the listing portal is more distant from the firm's core capabilities and customer workflows, management is more likely to see it as falling short of aspirations and reallocate its resources to core software and related innovation.
